_comment: Ground and road texture sets (CC0, ambientCG; data/credits.json texture_*). Engine-neutral: each layer names its colour / OpenGL normal / roughness maps; the renderer builds its texture arrays from them. tile_m = metres one texture repeat covers (a power of two, so the floating-origin offset can be taken modulo 1024 m). tint multiplies the colour map (the source sets are photographed brighter than a worn road). roughness = the layer's base roughness (the roughness maps are kept for engines that sample them). normal_strength scales the relief. Godot: game/scripts/surface_materials.gd, terrain.gdshader, road.gdshader.

terrain._comment: Natural ground (vertex kind 1): grass where the ramp colour is green (green minus red above greenness[0] blends in, fully grass at greenness[1]), dirt elsewhere, rock where the slope (1 - normal up) passes rock_slope[0], fully rock at rock_slope[1]. Paved / unpaved road vertices take paved / unpaved. macro: a second, large-scale lookup of the macro layer that varies the brightness by +-macro_strength so the repeats do not show. Beyond detail_far_m only the layers' mean colours are drawn (no texture lookups).

road._comment: Ribbon surfaces by road_visual.h flag: asphalt (none), concrete (4096), paving_stones (2048), sett (2048 + 16384: sett, cobblestone), unpaved (8192), verge (the gravel strip). Beyond detail_far_m the mean colour only.

flat_ground._comment: The flat test world's ground (one physics surface): this layer, with a painted grid of grid_line_width_m lines every grid_spacing_m metres.

wet._comment: Wet look (core rg/wet_look.h maps the physics water film and rain to wetness, puddles and drop density; these are the shading numbers): a fully wet surface keeps darken x its colour and its roughness drops to wet_roughness (natural ground: grass, soil and rock only to ground_wet_roughness, specular ground_wet_specular); puddles (flat spots picked by a large-scale noise, puddle_cover of the area at full puddles) are near mirrors (puddle_roughness) and darker still.
